message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance as international hubs:

| Airport | City | State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta | Georgia | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles | California | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and the Pacific; one of the busiest airports on the West Coast. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport | Chicago | Illinois | ORD | One of the oldest major hubs; key connecting point for United and American Airlines. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas/Fort Worth | Texas | DFW | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; major hub for American Airlines. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver | Colorado | DEN | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; major hub for United and Southwest Airlines. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City | New York | JFK | Major international gateway; hub for many airlines including Delta and JetBlue. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco | California | SFO | Key hub for flights to Asia and the Pacific; major focus city for United Airlines. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport | Seattle | Washington | SEA | Major hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami | Florida | MIA | Major hub for international flights to Latin America and the Caribbean. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix | Arizona | PHX | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest-growing airports in the U.S. |
| Orlando International Airport | Orlando | Florida | MCO | Major hub for leisure travel; key gateway for Walt Disney World and Universal Studios. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport | Newark | New Jersey | EWR | Major hub for United Airlines; important for flights to Europe and the Caribbean. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport | Charlotte | North Carolina | CLT | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest-growing airports in the U.S. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport | Washington, D.C. | Virginia | IAD | Major hub for United Airlines; key gateway to Europe and the Middle East. |

These airports serve as major hubs for domestic and international travel, handling millions of passengers each year and connecting the United States to the rest of the world.
